I've been through all 78 rules against the diff. One rule is broken, and I found two low-risk issues and one nit.

# Code-conventions review (`--review-pr` mode): `d78dc8e5…HEAD`

**Mode:** `--review-pr`. I generated the full all-rules checklist (78 rules, no project filter) and considered every rule. The checklist is a temporary file under the untracked `docs/engineering/`. I didn't tick its boxes because this was a read-only review. No tracked files were changed, and I didn't run any tests.

**Scope:** 19 new files under `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/Policies/SpendingLimitFlow/PolicySummary/`: components, copy and frequency helpers, test builders, tests and a Storybook story. All of it is additive and presentational, and nothing uses it yet.

## Findings

| # | Rule | Severity | Location | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **FEAT-01** Use feature public APIs across boundaries | Medium | `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/Policies/SpendingLimitFlow/PolicySummary/frequency.ts:1` | This file imports `getResetTimeOptions` from `@/features/spending-limits/constants`, which reaches into another feature's internals. The spending-limits barrel already exports it for cross-feature use (`features/spending-limits/index.ts`: `export { getResetTimeOptions } from './constants'`), and the only other outside consumer uses the barrel (`components/transactions/TxDetails/TxData/SpendingLimits/index.tsx:14`). ESLint doesn't catch this because it only restricts `components/`, `hooks/`, `services/*` and `store/*`. **Fix:** `import { getResetTimeOptions } from '@/features/spending-limits'`. |
| 2 | **SEC-01** Use own-property checks for map keys | Low | `.../PolicySummary/frequency.ts:16` (map at `.../PolicySummary/constants.ts:14`) | `CANONICAL_FREQUENCIES[resetTimeMin]` looks up a string key in a plain object literal. A key like `'constructor'` or `'toString'` finds an inherited value, so the canonical branch runs and returns `{ label: undefined }`. Today `resetTimeMin` comes from a dropdown, so this is unlikely. The model is meant to be built from form data later ("Phase 2"), though, and the rule asks for inherited keys to be impossible. **Fix:** guard with `Object.hasOwn(CANONICAL_FREQUENCIES, resetTimeMin)`, or use a `Map`. |
| 3 | **CODE-02** Extract repeated styling into named structure | Low | `.../PolicySummary/AppliesToRow.tsx:9-12` and `.../PolicySummary/SpenderSummaryCard.tsx:19-21` | The same shape is written twice: `<Card variant="muted" size="none" radius="lg">` wrapping a `div` with `p-3`, with the same explanatory comment in both places. One small local wrapper, such as `SummaryCard`, would state the padding decision once. |
| 4 | **TEST-01** Assertions must fail on the regression they claim to cover | Nit | `.../PolicySummary/__tests__/AppliesToRow.test.tsx:25` | The test title promises the fiat balance, but `toHaveTextContent('$')` passes for any fiat value, including `$0` or the wrong Safe's balance. It copies the existing `SafeAccountRow.test.tsx:50` pattern, so it is consistent with the repo, just weak. **Fix:** assert the formatted `123720` value. |

## Rules that applied and passed

- **FEAT-03:** imports inside the feature are relative, and nothing imports the feature's own barrel.
- **TEST-02 / TEST-03:** the pure helpers (`describeFrequency`, `describePolicy`, `joinNames`, `spenderDisplayName`) are tested separately from the components. Every branch has a test: mixed, uniform and test-chain periods, unnamed or blank names, an empty policy, unknown decimals and a failed parse.
- **TEST-05:** unit tests use colocated `Builder` factories and don't import from `config/test/msw/fixtures`. A second colocated `testBuilders.ts` already exists in `SpendingLimitFlow/utils/`, so there's precedent.
- **UI-01:** colors use theme tokens (`bg-muted-foreground/10`, `text-muted-foreground`), and the story uses hosted logo URLs.
- **NUM-01 / NUM-02:** no `Number` is serialised into a string for on-chain use. Amounts go through `safeParseUnits` with a fallback. The builder's float `toString()` stays at 0.0001 or above, so it never produces scientific notation.
- **DATA-05:** no address comparisons.
- **FEAT-04:** nothing under `components/ui/*` was changed.
- **CODE-01:** the new blocks reuse the selector's own row (`SafeAccountSummary`) plus the existing `EthHashInfo`, `TokenAmount` and `Alert` components, instead of forking them.
- **UX-01:** long spender names and addresses sit in `min-w-0` grid cells, and `EthHashInfo` handles truncation.
- **PROD-01:** the new visible copy is attributed to the Figma frame. One thing to confirm: the summary's labels ("One time only", "Weekly") deliberately differ from the form dropdown's ("One time", "1 week").

The other rules (auth, RTK, chain, mobile, CI, e2e, transactions, observability, docs and so on) don't touch anything in this diff.

## Outside the rules checklist

The root `AGENTS.md` says comments are tech debt and should be one line, only for the non-obvious. A few comments here go against that, and some will go out of date:
- `.../PolicySummary/index.tsx:9-12` refers to ticket WA-3152.
- `.../PolicySummary/types.ts:26` names `toPolicySummaryModel (Phase 2)`, which doesn't exist yet.
- `.../PolicySummary/copy.ts:36-39` and `.../PolicySummary/frequency.ts:11-14` are multi-line JSDoc blocks.

## Summary

- Checklist completed: all 78 rules considered.
- Rules that applied: FEAT-01, FEAT-03, SEC-01, CODE-01, CODE-02, TEST-01, TEST-02, TEST-03, TEST-05, UI-01, NUM-01, NUM-02, DATA-05, UX-01, PROD-01.
- Rule failed: FEAT-01. Low-risk issues: SEC-01 and CODE-02. Nit: TEST-01.
- I didn't need to look up past review feedback (Level 1 or 2 zoom) for any rule.
- Nothing was changed, since this was a review only.
